North Richmond Street, being a dead end, was a quiet street except at the hour when the Christian Brothers School set the boys free. <break time="0.8s" /> At the blind end stood an uninhabited house of two storeys, detached from its neighbours on a square ground. <break time="0.8s" /> The other houses of the street, conscious of decent lives within them, gazed at one another with brown, imperturbable faces. <break time="0.8s" /> The former tenant of our house, a priest, had died in the back drawing room, and the air, musty from having been long enclosed, hung in all the rooms. <break time="0.8s" /> Among the useless papers in the waste room behind the kitchen, I found a few old books whose pages were curled and damp. <break time="0.8s" /> He had been a very charitable priest, for in his will he had left all his money to institutions and the furniture of his house to his sister. <break time="0.8s" /> When the short days of winter came, dusk fell before we had well eaten our dinners, and we played in the dark, muddy lanes behind the houses. <break time="0.8s" /> If Mangans sister came out on the doorstep to call her brother in to his tea, we watched her from our shadow peering up and down the street.

Every morning I lay on the floor in the front parlour watching her door, keeping the blind pulled down to within an inch of the sash so that I could not be seen. <break time="0.8s" /> When she came out on the doorstep, my heart leaped, and I ran to the hall, seized my books, and followed her, always keeping her brown figure in my eye. <break time="0.8s" /> I had never spoken to her, except for a few casual words, and yet her name was like a summons to all my foolish blood. <break time="0.8s" /> Her image accompanied me even in places the most hostile to romance, such as the crowded market where my aunt went shopping on Saturday evenings. <break time="0.8s" /> We walked through the flaring streets, jostled by drunken men and bargaining women, amid the curses of labourers and the shrill cries of shop boys. <break time="0.8s" /> These noises converged in a single sensation of life for me, and I imagined that I bore my chalice safely through a throng of foes. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening I went into the back drawing room in which the priest had died, and it was a dark, rainy evening, and there was no sound in the house. <break time="0.8s" /> Pressing the palms of my hands together until they trembled, I murmured, O love, O love, many times.
